For the latency-sensitive interaction scenario, the system enables a lightweight fast mode: it directly reads out the structure of 𝒯 N \mathcal{T}_{N} along with the non-empty leaf texts as a personalized prior, concatenates them with the user query q q as the input context, and generates an answer in a single pass. When the user explicitly requests additional details or the query exhibits stronger long-tail characteristics, the system switches to the agentic recall mode. Concretely, we generate a set of expanded queries { q ~ ( k ) } k = 1 K \{\tilde{q}^{(k)}\}_{k=1}^{K} from the original query q q conditioned on 𝒯 N \mathcal{T}_{N} , where each q ~ ( k ) \tilde{q}^{(k)} emphasizes a different attribute dimension or potential missing aspect relevant to the question. The system retrieves candidate evidence sets { d j ( k ) } \{d^{(k)}_{j}\} in parallel for { q ( k ) } \{q^{(k)}\} , and reranks them based on relevance to obtain a fused context C C . Finally, we generate the final answer conditioned on [ q , 𝒯 N , C ] [q,\,\mathcal{T}_{N},\,C] . This procedure operates under a gated policy that is triggered only when necessary, improving answer quality in complex scenarios while keeping the overall interaction cost controllable. We conduct experiments on the PersonaMem benchmark [ jiang2025know ] .
